1. Increasing the learning rate should help more when it starts low, since low rates undertrain in 243 epochs. Small batch sizes give many more updates per epoch, which makes low learning rates less of a problem, so a larger learning rate should help more when the batch size is large.
2. A larger batch size means fewer updates, so raising it should hurt more when the learning rate is low.
3. At a high learning rate (0.0774 to 1), training is unstable, so raising it further should hurt more than at other bands.
4. Raising the learning rate when the batch size is small (4 to 10) is risky because the gradient noise is large, so the effect should be lower.
5. Increasing width should help more when depth is 1, because shallow networks are capacity-limited.
6. Increasing alpha at the high band (0.129 to 1) strongly over-regularizes, so raising it further should be lower.
7. Increasing alpha should hurt more when width is small, since there is less capacity to spare.
8. Increasing depth should hurt more when the learning rate is high, since deep networks diverge more easily.
9. Increasing width should help more when the learning rate is low, since wider networks train faster at a low learning rate.
10. Decreasing batch size should help more when the learning rate is low, since more updates compensate for the slow learning.
